headline: Poland has received the first batch of South Korean K2 Black Panther tanks under its latest $6.7 billion defense deal with Hyundai Rotem. Under the second contract, Poland is acquiring 180 K2 tanks. The first 28 vehicles have already been delivered and assigned to the 16th Pomeranian Mechanized Division. This brings Poland’s K2 fleet to 208 tanks. The new deliveries are part of Poland’s broader military rearmament program, launched following the outbreak of the war in Ukraine and focused on rapidly expanding the country’s fleet of modern armored vehicles. The first contract covered 180 K2GF tanks, all of which Poland received by the end of 2025. The second phase now focuses on gradually increasing the local production and integration of the K2 platform. Under the latest agreement, Poland will receive: • 116 K2GF tanks in 2026–2027; • 64 K2PL tanks in 2028–2030. The K2PL is tailored to the requirements of the Polish Army and features a greater share of domestic production. Of the 64 K2PLs, 61 are expected to be assembled in Poland at the Bumar-Łabędy plant in Gliwice using Polish components. The contract also includes a comprehensive support package comprising: • 25 K2-based armored engineering vehicles; • 25 armored bridge layers; • 31 repair and recovery vehicles; • ammunition; • personnel training; • technology transfer.

The claim of mass killings appears to refer to the January 2026 nationwide protests, when Iranian security forces carried out a major crackdown in which several thousand were killed. There have not been credible reports of a comparable new mass killing of protesters in recent weeks. Iran has, however, continued its crackdown through arrests, executions and prosecutions of people accused of participating in the January protests. The European Union and 26 other countries condemned Iran's execution of protesters earlier this month. President Trump's comments come as his administration has sharply escalated pressure on Tehran, most recently announcing Operation Economic Outcast, an effort to isolate Iran economically and cut off remaining financial lifelines.
summary: President Donald J. Trump has posted to Truth Social stating that Iran is failing to pay "large segments of their military" and is "killing protesters...at levels not seen before," describing the situation as a "humanitarian crisis of epic proportions" that "must be stopped, NOW.

headline: A U.S. Air Force C-17A "Globemaster III", operating under callsign RCH4555, has landed at Vnukovo Airport in Moscow, marking the first publicly observed U.S. Air Force C-17 arrival in Russia since May 2020, when a C-17 delivered ventilators during the COVID-19 pandemic. The aircraft arrived in Moscow from Riga, Latvia, after having flown to Riga from Joint Base Andrews near Washington, D.C., on August 23. Flight tracking data indicates the mission is likely connected to an upcoming trip by Secretary of War Pete Hegseth, although that remains unconfirmed. The C-17 is frequently used to preposition personnel, vehicles and equipment ahead of senior-level travel, but it can also serve as transportation for the Secretary of War on sensitive or unannounced missions.

headline: Mike Rogers, the Republican nominee for Senate in Michigan, attended a total of, not one, not two, but three fundraisers hosted by the American Israel Public Affairs Committee (AIPAC) in Los Angeles on Sunday, as well as another which was planned for Monday, according to The New York Times. AIPAC, a powerful lobbying group for Israel in the United States, that is facing growing animosity in the Democratic Party from progressive critics of Israel, has spent weeks preparing to start an ad campaign to support Rogers, despite concerns from Rogers and his allies that support from the group could politically backfire in Michigan. AIPAC spent $32 million through its main super PAC, the United Democracy Project, in an unsuccessful effort to defeat Dr. Abdul El-Sayed, a vocal critic of Israel and AIPAC, in Michigan’s Democratic Senate Primary. This month, which the super PAC entered with $59 million in its account, it took the extraordinary step of making plans to spend on behalf of Mr. Rogers, who has long been supportive of Israel, and against Dr. El-Sayed.
